Yesterday there were reports that Apple had considered creating a special version of the Apple Pencil for the upcoming iPhone Ultra, but ultimately shelved the related plans.

Bloomberg pointed out three reasons why Apple abandoned this idea, one of which is concern about contradicting the stance held by Steve Jobs when he launched the first-generation iPhone. However, this is almost certainly not the most important deciding factor...

A short Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra sounds theoretically quite appealing. The device is essentially an iPhone that can transform into an iPad mini, so giving it some similar functions also seems to make sense.

When Samsung launched the Galaxy Note tablet-phone in 2011, it came with an S-Pen stylus. The concept at the time was that this device could partially replace a paper notebook, and this product line lasted for ten years, with a loyal user base, until production ceased in 2021.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman listed three reasons why Apple ultimately abandoned this idea:

  • Storing the Pencil on the side of the device rather than the top would feel awkward when holding it
  • This runs counter to Steve's view that a stylus is merely an inferior substitute for the finger
  • It would leave unsightly marks on the screen

I don't think the first reason is the main consideration, because mounting the stylus on the top of the device is also a feasible option. Although this would require an extremely compact design, I believe it is still doable.

I also have reservations about the second reason. What Steve objected to back then was not the concept that smartphones could use a stylus, but rather that the models at the time had to rely on a stylus to operate. Being able to operate the iPhone nimbly with the finger was the real breakthrough.

In any case, Steve had also publicly opposed adding a touchscreen to the Mac on ergonomic grounds in the past, but we currently still expect the upcoming MacBook Pro models to include touch functionality, showing that Apple is not averse to overturning the stance of its co-founder.

I think what truly killed this idea is the third reason. The surface of a folding screen is inevitably thinner and more flexible than existing devices. Reports indicate that Apple has delayed the launch of its first folding iPhone precisely because of concerns about the screen's appearance and durability; if the Apple Pencil were to repeatedly scratch the surface, it would affect both aspects simultaneously.

If Apple ultimately manages to solve this problem, would you like to see an Apple Pencil Mini designed specifically for the future iPhone Ultra? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
